name: Maureen
title: 12-Week Return-to-Fitness Plan - Maureen
intro: 4 days per week (Day 1-4, any days you like): 3 full-body strength days + 1 cardio day, about 35-45 minutes. Strength days end with 10-15 min of easy bike or incline walking. Everything starts conservatively and adjusts week by week from your results.

warmup.label: 1. Get warm (3 min)
warmup.text: Easy bike or treadmill walk, gradually picking up the pace.

warmup.label: 2. Mobility (2 min)
warmup.text: 10 cat-cows, 10 bodyweight squats to the bench, 10 hip hinges (hands on hips, push hips back), 10 arm circles each way, 10 glute bridges.

warmup.label: 3. Ramp-up set (1 min)
warmup.text: Before the first exercise: 1 light set of 6-8 reps (empty handle or no weight) focusing on form.

cooldown.label: Cool-down (3-5 min)
cooldown.text: Easy walk, then gentle stretches held 20-30 sec, no bouncing: hip flexors (half-kneeling), hamstrings, glutes (figure-4), calves, chest in a doorway, child's pose.

items.label: Starting point
items.text: Getting back into working out. Goals, preferred days, health history and current fitness aren't known yet - so the plan deliberately starts light and simple. The first weeks are about learning the moves and building the habit.

items.label: Goal (assumed)
items.text: Get back into a steady routine; build full-body strength (legs, glutes, back, arms, core) with good form; improve cardio fitness and energy. If your goals are different (e.g., more cardio, weight loss, a sport or an event), tell Coach and the plan will be adjusted.

items.label: Targets adjust weekly
items.text: Every target is a SUGGESTION. Week 1 is a BASELINE week: the weights, reps and cardio numbers you log become your starting point, and future targets are adjusted from what you send back each week (EASY / OK / HARD and your notes).

items.label: Phases
items.text:
Weeks 1-4: FOUNDATION (learn the movements, light loads, 2-3 sets; lighter deload week 4)
Weeks 5-8: BUILD (3 sets, small load increases, longer cardio with incline; lighter deload week 8)
Weeks 9-12: STRENGTHEN (slightly heavier sets of 8-10, gentle bike intervals; week 12 = RETEST week: 'see how far you've come' - rep and cardio benchmarks vs. week 1, NO one-rep max).

items.label: Days
items.text: 4 sessions per week, no fixed weekdays - do them in order: Day 1 Strength A, Day 2 Cardio, Day 3 Strength B, Day 4 Strength C. Each session takes about 35-45 minutes.

items.label: Rest days
items.text: Leave at least one rest day between strength days when possible (the cardio day can sit in between). Example: Mon Strength A, Tue Cardio, Thu Strength B, Sat Strength C. Missed a day? Just pick up where you left off - don't double up.

items.label: Strength A (Day 1)
items.text: Goblet squat | Incline push-up (bar in rack) | Lat pulldown | Glute bridge | Dead bug | 10-15 min easy cardio finisher.

items.label: Cardio (Day 2)
items.text: Zone 2 (conversational) bike or treadmill walk: 20-25 min to start, building to 35-40 min, adding incline walking from week 5 and gentle bike intervals in weeks 7 and 10.

items.label: Strength B (Day 3)
items.text: Romanian deadlift | Low cable row | Dumbbell overhead press (seated) | Split squat | Pallof press | 10-15 min easy cardio finisher.

items.label: Strength C (Day 4)
items.text: Hip thrust | Goblet squat with 2-sec pause | Landmine press | One-arm low cable row | Plank | 10-15 min easy cardio finisher.

items.label: Session length (35-45 min)
items.text: 5-min warm-up + 20-25 min of strength (rest 60-90 sec between sets) + 10-15 min easy cardio finisher + a short cool-down. To save time, pair a lower-body and an upper-body exercise and alternate them.

items.label: 1. Get warm (3 min)
items.text: Easy bike or treadmill walk, gradually picking up the pace.

items.label: 2. Mobility (2 min)
items.text: 10 cat-cows, 10 bodyweight squats to the bench, 10 hip hinges (hands on hips, push hips back), 10 arm circles each way, 10 glute bridges.

items.label: 3. Ramp-up set (1 min)
items.text: Before the first exercise: 1 light set of 6-8 reps (empty handle or no weight) focusing on form.

items.label: Cool-down (3-5 min)
items.text: Easy walk, then gentle stretches held 20-30 sec, no bouncing: hip flexors (half-kneeling), hamstrings, glutes (figure-4), calves, chest in a doorway, child's pose.

items.label: Strength: RPE 6-7
items.text: Finish each set feeling like you could do 2-3 more good reps. Never train to failure. Slow, controlled reps: about 2-3 seconds down, controlled up, breathe out on the effort (don't hold your breath).

items.label: EASY / OK / HARD
items.text: EASY = could have done 4+ more reps, form solid. OK = 2-3 reps left (the target). HARD = only 0-1 reps left or form got shaky. Circle one for each session - it drives next week's targets.

items.label: Cardio: Zone 2
items.text: Talk test: you can speak in full sentences (about 3-5 out of 10 effort). 'Moderate' on interval days = short phrases only (about 6/10). Never all-out.

items.label: Effort scale (1-10)
items.text: 1-2 very easy, 3-4 easy/conversational, 5-6 moderate, 7-8 hard, 9-10 all-out (never in this plan).

items.label: How it works
items.text: Each exercise has a rep target (e.g., 3 x 10-12). Keep the same weight until ALL sets feel EASY at the top of the range with good form, then add a small amount (2.5-5 lb) next time. If a set is HARD or form slips, stay at that weight (or go lighter).

items.label: Load shorthand
items.text: H = one EMPTY plate-loading dumbbell handle. WEIGH ONE before week 1 (bathroom scale): ______ lb (often 3-6 lb). 'H+10' = handle with a 5 lb plate on each end. 'H+15*' = add a 2.5 lb plate on each end. '2 handles, each H+10' = one in each hand.

items.label: Small jumps need 2.5s
items.text: Targets marked * need the 2.5 lb plates (recommended purchase). Without them, stay at the previous weight and add 1-2 reps per set instead - the 5 lb plates make 10 lb jumps on a handle, which is too big a step.

items.label: Machines
items.text: Lat pulldown and low cable row: the empty carriage has its own resistance. In week 1, start with nothing loaded and add 5 lb at a time until 12 reps feel about 6-7/10 - write that weight down; it's your start weight.

items.label: Bodyweight moves
items.text: Incline push-ups get harder by lowering the bar one hole at a time (when all sets reach 12 EASY reps). Planks and dead bugs progress with time/reps; split squats move from bodyweight to two handles.

items.label: Cardio
items.text: Add a few minutes each week (20 -> 40 min), then a little treadmill incline (weeks 5-6, 9) and gentle 1-min bike intervals (weeks 7 and 10). Stay conversational except during the short moderate intervals.

items.label: Deload weeks 4 and 8
items.text: Lighter on purpose: 2 sets instead of 3 and/or lighter weights, shorter cardio. Lets your body catch up so you come back stronger. Don't skip them and don't make them harder.

items.label: Week 12 - retest
items.text: Light strength sessions plus the same tests as week 1: max clean incline push-ups at the same bar height, longest good-form plank, and the 20-minute cardio test on the same machine and settings. Also compare your week-2 and week-11 weights on the Progress Log. NO one-rep max tests.

items.label: Targets
items.text: Targets in the plan are SUGGESTIONS ONLY. Your weekly results (weights, reps, EASY/OK/HARD and notes) decide the next week's targets.

items.label: Check with your doctor
items.text: Before starting, check with your doctor if you have ANY health condition (heart, blood pressure, diabetes, asthma), take medication that affects heart rate or balance, are pregnant or postpartum, have joint/back problems or a past injury, or simply haven't exercised in a long time.

items.label: Stop for pain
items.text: Stop the exercise for sharp pain or any joint pain (knees, back, hips, shoulders, wrists). Normal muscle burn and mild soreness 1-2 days later are OK; pain is not. Skip that move and tell Coach.

items.label: Warning signs
items.text: Stop immediately and seek medical help for chest pain or pressure, dizziness or light-headedness, unusual shortness of breath, irregular heartbeat, or feeling faint.

items.label: Form first
items.text: If form breaks down, end the set. Leave 2-3 reps in the tank. Slow and controlled - no bouncing, jerking or swinging.

items.label: No max testing
items.text: No one-rep max (1RM) tests. Progress is measured with reps, holds, weights used for sets, and cardio time/distance.

items.label: Rack safeties set
items.text: Keep the power rack safeties set (pins locked) for incline push-ups and whenever the bar is in the rack. Take the RDL bar from the rack hooks, not the floor.

items.label: Recovery
items.text: Sleep 7-9 hours, drink water before/during/after, eat protein at each meal. Mild soreness is normal early on - an easy walk helps.

items.label: Environment
items.text: Clear floor space, stable shoes, collars on the bar, no loose plates on the floor, treadmill safety clip attached.

items.label: Mikolo F4 power rack + safeties
items.text: Incline push-up station: bar on the J-hooks/safeties at hip height to start, lowered one hole at a time. Hold the upright for balance on split squats. Safeties always set.

items.label: Plate-loaded lat pulldown & low cable row
items.text: Lat pulldown, low cable row, one-arm row and the Pallof press (side-on to the low-row cable). Start with nothing loaded and write the carriage weight: ___ lb.

items.label: Landmine
items.text: Landmine press with the 45 lb Olympic bar (you only lift part of the bar's weight). Start with both hands; one arm from week 5.

items.label: Flat bench + leg extension attachment
items.text: Bench = hip thrust support, seated overhead press, squat depth target. Leg extension is not in the plan (optional later).

items.label: 35 lb bar
items.text: Romanian deadlift from week 5 and hip thrust (padded with a towel) from week 9.

items.label: 45 lb Olympic bar
items.text: Landmine only.

items.label: EZ curl bar, pull-up bar, dip handles
items.text: Not used in this plan (optional extras later: EZ-bar curls, dead hangs).

items.label: Plate-loading dumbbell handles
items.text: Weigh one empty handle: ______ lb. Used for goblet squats, RDLs (weeks 1-4), split squats and overhead press.

items.label: Plates on hand
items.text: 2 x 45 lb, 4 x 10 lb, 4 x 5 lb. That allows H+10 (5s), H+20 (10s), H+30 (10s + 5s) and 2 handles at H+10 each. Smaller steps need 2.5 lb plates.

items.label: Fixed dumbbells 25s and 45s
items.text: 25 lb: goblet squat (weeks 10-12) and hip thrust (weeks 5-7). 45 lb: optional hip thrust in week 11 only if EASY.

items.label: Indoor bike + treadmill
items.text: Cardio day and the 10-15 min finisher after strength days. Note the machine, speed/incline or resistance each time so progress is comparable.

items.label: No TRX
items.text: Not needed; the cable stations and rack cover pulling and the Pallof press.

items.label: Pair of 2.5 lb plates (2 pairs ideal)
items.text: Recommended. Allows +5 lb steps on a handle (2.5 each end) and on the bar, and +2.5 lb on the cable stations. Very low cost; makes the * targets possible.

items.label: Hip thrust pad or folded towel
items.text: For comfort when the 35 lb bar sits on the hips (weeks 9-12).

items.label: Nice to have: 1.25 lb plates
items.text: Even smaller steps for the overhead press.

guide.name: Cat-cow (warm-up)
guide.how: On hands and knees. Slowly round the back up toward the ceiling (cat), then let the belly drop and lift the chest (cow). Move with your breath, 10 slow reps.

guide.name: Hip hinge drill (warm-up)
guide.how: Hands on hips, soft knees. Push the hips straight back until you feel the back of the legs stretch, keep a flat back, then stand tall by squeezing the glutes. This is the RDL pattern.

guide.name: Goblet squat
guide.how: Hold one dumbbell handle vertically against the chest with both hands. Feet about shoulder width, toes slightly out. Sit down between the heels as deep as you comfortably can with the chest up and heels down (touch the bench first if helpful), then stand tall. Day C version: pause 2 sec at the bottom.

guide.name: Incline push-up (bar in rack)
guide.how: Set the bar on the J-hooks or safeties at hip height (pins locked). Hands a bit wider than shoulders, walk the feet back until the body is a straight line. Lower the chest to the bar, push away. Lower the bar one hole when 12 reps feel EASY on all sets. Higher bar = easier.

guide.name: Lat pulldown
guide.how: Grip a little wider than shoulders, thighs under the pad if there is one. Sit tall, pull the bar to the upper chest by driving the elbows down and back, without leaning way back or yanking. Let it rise slowly.

guide.name: Glute bridge
guide.how: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width. Ribs down, push through the heels and squeeze the glutes until knees, hips and shoulders line up; pause and lower. Single-leg: one foot lifted, same thing.

guide.name: Dead bug
guide.how: Lie on your back, arms reaching to the ceiling, knees bent at 90 degrees over the hips. Press the low back gently into the floor. Slowly reach the opposite arm and leg out while breathing out, return, switch.

guide.name: Romanian deadlift (RDL)
guide.how: Start STANDING with the weight (bar from the rack hooks at mid-thigh, or a handle in each hand). Soft knees, push the hips back, let the weight slide down the thighs to just below the knees with a flat back and neck in line, then stand by squeezing the glutes. Feel it in the hamstrings, not the low back.

guide.name: Low cable row
guide.how: Sit tall with a slight knee bend, chest up. Pull the handle to the belly while squeezing the shoulder blades together, then let the arms straighten slowly without rounding forward.

guide.name: Dumbbell overhead press (seated)
guide.how: Sit tall on the bench, feet flat, ribs down. Handles at shoulder height, palms facing forward or in. Press straight up until the arms are by the ears, lower slowly. No arching the low back.

guide.name: Split squat
guide.how: Long stance, feet hip-width apart (like train tracks, not a tightrope). Lower the back knee gently toward the floor, front knee over the middle of the foot, torso tall, push through the front heel to rise. Hold the rack for balance. Do all reps, then switch legs.

guide.name: Pallof press (low row cable)
guide.how: Kneel tall or stand side-on to the low-row cable with the handle at the middle of the chest. Brace and press the handle straight out, hold 2 sec without letting the cable twist you, bring it back. All reps one side, then turn around. Substitute: side plank on the knees, 2 x 15-20 sec/side.

guide.name: Hip thrust (shoulders on bench)
guide.how: Sit on the floor with the upper back against the long side of the bench, knees bent, feet flat. Weight (dumbbell or padded bar) across the hip crease. Chin tucked, drive through the heels to lift the hips until level with knees and shoulders, squeeze 1 sec, lower under control.

guide.name: Landmine press
guide.how: 45 lb bar in the landmine. Hold the bar end at the chest (both hands to start; later one hand, half-kneeling or standing). Press up and forward until the arm is straight, lower slowly. Ribs down, glutes tight, no leaning back.

guide.name: One-arm low cable row
guide.how: Single handle on the low-row cable. Seated or half-kneeling, pull to the hip, squeeze the shoulder blade back, slow return. All reps, then switch arms.

guide.name: Plank
guide.how: Forearms on the floor under the shoulders, body straight from head to heels, glutes and belly tight, keep breathing. Knees down to make it easier. End the set when the hips sag or the low back arches.

guide.name: Zone 2 cardio (bike or treadmill walk)
guide.how: Easy, steady effort where you can speak in full sentences (about 3-5/10). Warm up 3-5 min, cool down 3-5 min. Log minutes, machine, speed/incline or resistance, and effort 1-10 so progress is comparable week to week.

guide.name: Incline walk
guide.how: Treadmill walk at an easy pace with 2-8% incline. Stand tall; hold the rails only for balance, not to lean on. Lower the incline if calves or shins complain.

guide.name: Gentle bike intervals
guide.how: After an easy warm-up, alternate 1 min moderate (about 6/10, short phrases only) with 2 min easy. Never all-out. Finish with easy pedaling.

guide.name: Cardio finisher
guide.how: After strength days: 10-15 min of easy bike or incline treadmill walking (zone 2). Log minutes, machine, setting and effort.

guide.name: Benchmark tests (week 1 and week 12)
guide.how: Max clean incline push-ups at the same bar hole, longest good-form plank, and a 20-min zone 2 cardio test on the same machine and settings (record distance and effort). Stop every test 1-2 reps before form breaks. No one-rep maxes.

exercises.name: Split squat
